channel.title: PsyDigest — psychiatry literature digest
channel.description: Summaries of new psychiatric research and guidelines

item.title: Intensified return to work clinical aftercare for sick-listed employees with diagnosed mental disorders in Germany: effects of a multicentre randomized controlled trial.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: A multicentre RCT in German psychiatric outpatient clinics (N = 484 sick-listed employees with mental disorders) tested an 18-month intensified return-to-work aftercare program (RTW-PIA) added to care-as-usual (CAU) versus CAU alone, with primary outcome sustainable RTW (≤ 6 weeks sickness absence within 12 months after full RTW) and secondary outcomes over 24 months.
FINDINGS: The primary outcome showed no significant effect of RTW-PIA (OR 1.38, 95 % CI 0.89–2.12). Secondary outcomes were largely unchanged; only employees with recurrent depressive disorders showed improvements in several secondary measures. Prespecified moderator analyses suggested possible benefits for those without recognized disability degree and for those with low workplace social support, but after multiplicity adjustment only recurrent depressive disorder remained a significant moderator for work ability.
INTERPRETATION: The trial has high internal validity (randomised, multicentre, prespecified analyses) but the overall null result for the primary outcome and most secondary outcomes argues against broad effectiveness of RTW-PIA in its current form. Subgroup findings are exploratory and require independent replication before clinical adoption. The programme’s implementation challenges and resource demands are not addressed.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: At present, RTW-PIA cannot be recommended for routine use to improve sustainable return to work in unselected sick-listed psychiatric patients; targeted trials in recurrent depression and low social support subgroups are needed before any change in practice.

item.title: Effectiveness of a nurse-led telephonic brief intervention to reduce risky alcohol use among women in primary care in Brazil: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study addressed whether a nurse-led telephonic brief intervention (BI) can reduce risky alcohol use among women in Brazilian primary care, a setting where gender-responsive, scalable interventions are scarce. It was a randomized controlled trial (RCT) with 151 women scoring 8–19 on the AUDIT.
FINDINGS: Over the first 6 months, AUDIT scores fell in the intervention group (IG) while rising in controls; the between-group difference was statistically significant (effect size not reported). By 24 months, the initial benefit in the IG attenuated and the control group’s scores continued to increase. Socioeconomic factors (race, household income) were associated with AUDIT trajectories.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence is moderate: the RCT design and longitudinal follow-up strengthen internal validity, but the lack of effect-size estimates and blinding of assessors limits precision. The short-lived benefit suggests a single BI is insufficient for long-term change; booster sessions may be needed. External validity is constrained by the single-city, female-only sample and resource-constrained primary-care context.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: A nurse-delivered telephonic BI can produce modest short-term reductions in risky drinking for women in primary care, but sustained impact is unlikely without additional support; services should plan for follow-up or booster contacts.

item.title: Changes in resting-state functional connectivity between large-scale brain networks after an intensive arts intervention for adolescents with depression.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This prospective cohort study examined whether a two-week intensive arts intervention (Creativity Camp) altered resting-state functional connectivity (rs-FC) between large-scale brain networks in 39 adolescents with depression, and whether any changes correlated with symptom improvement. The study used graph theory to quantify between-network connectivity among Default, Control, Salience, and Limbic networks before and after the intervention, with a partial waitlist comparison.
FINDINGS: In the whole sample, connectivity strength increased significantly from pre- to post-camp for three network pairs: Default-Control (p < 0.05, corrected), Limbic-Control (p < 0.05, corrected), and Salience-Default (p < 0.05, corrected). In the waitlist-controlled comparison, changes during camp exceeded those during the two-week waitlist for two of these pairs (uncorrected). However, no significant correlations were found between changes in connectivity and changes in depressive symptoms (no effect sizes or p-values reported).
INTERPRETATION: The study provides preliminary evidence that a brief, intensive arts intervention may enhance connectivity between networks implicated in mood regulation and creativity. However, the lack of blinding, small sample size, and absence of a true randomized control group limit causal inference. The waitlist comparison was underpowered and reported uncorrected results, raising the risk of false positives. The absence of correlation with symptom change further limits clinical interpretation. Larger randomized trials with longer follow-up are needed to determine whether these neural changes are mechanistically or therapeutically meaningful.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: At present, this study does not support changes in clinical practice. While the neural findings are intriguing, they are not linked to symptom improvement and require replication in more rigorous trials before any treatment implications can be considered.

item.title: Perinatal Bipolar Disorder Management: Lithium in the Setting of Obstetric Complications.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The abstract describes a case report highlighting the challenges of managing lithium treatment in a pregnant woman with bipolar I disorder, particularly when obstetric complications (e.g., preeclampsia) arise. The focus is on balancing psychiatric and obstetric risks in perinatal bipolar disorder management.
FINDINGS: The case involves a 37-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder whose lithium levels unexpectedly rose during pregnancy, preceding the onset of preeclampsia. The report underscores the variability in clinical practice among reproductive psychiatrists regarding lithium monitoring and management in the peripartum period.
INTERPRETATION: As a case report, the evidence is anecdotal and lacks generalizability. The findings are preliminary and do not establish causality or provide quantitative data. The study highlights a potential association between elevated lithium levels and preeclampsia, but this requires further investigation in larger, controlled studies to confirm any clinical significance.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This case report serves as a reminder to monitor lithium levels closely in pregnant patients with bipolar disorder, particularly in the context of obstetric complications. However, it does not provide definitive guidance for practice changes, and clinicians should rely on broader evidence-based guidelines for now.

item.title: Cognitive Effects of Cenobamate as Compared to Perampanel: A Cross-Sectional Multicentre Study in 600 Patients.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study compared cognitive performance (executive functions) in 600 adults with epilepsy treated with cenobamate (CNB) versus perampanel (PER), an antiseizure medication (ASM) without systematic negative cognitive effects. It used a retrospective cross-sectional multicentre design with matched samples.
FINDINGS: The analysis included 200 CNB-treated patients (mean dose 190.9 mg/day) and 400 PER-treated patients (mean dose 7.1 mg/day). Bayesian ANOVA found no difference in executive function performance between groups (Bayes Factor [BF] = 0.207), but strong evidence of worse cognition with more concomitant ASMs (BF = 9.5 × 10⁶). The mean age was 38.7 years, and 48.5% were women.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence is moderate-strength due to the cross-sectional design and lack of randomisation or blinding. The large BF favours no cognitive difference between CNB and PER, but the study did not assess episodic memory or dose-dependent effects. Confounding by indication or unmeasured variables cannot be ruled out. The strong association with polytherapy is consistent with prior literature.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: CNB and PER appear comparable in their effects on executive function, but clinicians should remain cautious about cognitive side effects in patients on multiple ASMs. Further prospective or randomised studies are needed to confirm these findings and assess other cognitive domains.

item.title: Demographic, history, university and lifestyle factors associated with university student mental health: cross-sectional analysis across five UK universities.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This cross-sectional study across five UK universities (2022–2024) examined demographic, university, and lifestyle factors associated with student mental health and well-being, aiming to inform whole-university mental health strategies.
FINDINGS: Of 14,172 students, >25% screened positive for probable anxiety or depression (PHQ-9/GAD-7 thresholds). Younger age, female/LGBTQIA+ identity, and disability were associated with worse mental health. University-specific factors (course or institution) showed minimal impact. Exercise and self-care were strongly associated with better well-being (SWEMWBS) and lower depression/anxiety.
INTERPRETATION: The large sample size strengthens precision, but the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. Self-reported data may introduce bias, and unmeasured confounders (e.g., socioeconomic status) could influence associations. The effect sizes for lifestyle factors (e.g., exercise) are modest but consistent, suggesting potential utility in interventions. However, the lack of university-specific impact limits actionable targets beyond general health promotion.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Universities may prioritize promoting exercise and self-care to support student mental health, but should avoid overemphasizing course/institution-level changes based on these findings. Further longitudinal or interventional research is needed to confirm causality.

item.title: Integrating Wearable Technology in Digital Therapy for People With Psychosis (SloMo): Mixed Methods Co-Design and Feasibility Study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Digital health interventions for psychosis, like SloMo, leverage smartphone technology to help transfer learning from therapy to real-life situations. Usage relies on motivation, recall, and awareness. Wearable devices that track physiological signs of stress can boost engagement by encouraging the use of coping strategies when most needed.

item.title: Unseen and underserved: A scoping review of perinatal mental health interventions in Sub-Saharan Africa.
item.description: Maternal mental health (MMH) remains a critical public health issue across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Despite the high burden, access to culturally appropriate and evidence-based mental health interventions remains limited. This scoping review examines interventions targeting mental health outcomes for pregnant and postpartum women across SSA countries. Guided by PRISMA-ScR and Arksey and O'Malley's framework, a comprehensive search was conducted across 14 electronic databases for peer-reviewed intervention studies published in English between 2000 and March 2026.

item.title: Loneliness as a risk factor for bipolar disorder and its related brain structure alterations.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Loneliness has been linked to increased risk of mood disorders, but its relationship with bipolar disorder (BD) and underlying neurobiological mechanisms remain unclear. METHODS: This prospective cohort study utilized data from the UK Biobank, involving 491,472 individuals aged 38-73 years without prior BD diagnosis at baseline (2006-2010). Participants reported loneliness and provided data on demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle factors, and polygenic risk scores (PRS) for BD. Follow-up extended until 2022, tracking incident BD cases.

item.title: Coordinated response of vascular and glial cells in a pig model of sepsis.
item.description: Sepsis is a deadly syndrome arising from overactivation of the immune system in response to a pathogen. Severe sepsis can result in sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) that significantly contributes to morbidity and long-term cognitive impairment. Studying the molecular underpinnings of SAE in the human brain is challenging, and rodent models have limited translational applicability due to significant neuroanatomical and immune differences.

item.title: Narrative exposure therapy for war-affected Middle Eastern refugees: a scoping review of outcomes, delivery contexts and implementation gaps.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Refugees from the Middle East are exposed to multiple war-related and displacement-related stressors. Narrative Exposure Therapy (NET) and its child-adapted version (KIDNET) have been applied in various settings, but evidence remains scattered. OBJECTIVE: To map the available evidence on NET/KIDNET among war-affected Middle Eastern refugees, focusing on outcomes, delivery contexts, study designs, and implementation gaps. METHODS: Peer-reviewed articles were systematically reviewed by screening three electronic databases: PubMed, ScienceDirect and Scopus.

item.title: Psychoeducation for Youth at Clinical High-Risk of Psychosis.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Psychoeducation may be a useful first-step intervention for youth at clinical high risk of developing psychosis (CHR). The aim of this study was to describe clinical improvement after receiving psychoeducation and adherence to the treatment. METHODS: The study included 54 participants who began the treatment and 48 completed a follow-up assessment 2-6 months after baseline. Clinical assessments included measures of attenuated psychotic symptoms (APS), negative symptoms, depression, anxiety, distress and social and role functioning.

item.title: Duration of Medication Use for Opioid Use Disorder and Risk of Postpartum Overdose and Death.
item.description: IMPORTANCE: Overdose is the leading cause of maternal mortality in the US, yet evidence on how medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) affect postpartum overdose and mortality risk is limited. It is unclear whether cumulative MOUD exposure during this period reduces overdose or death beyond 90 days post partum. OBJECTIVE: To examine whether longer duration of MOUD dispensed during pregnancy and early post partum is associated with reduced overdose or death through 365 days post partum.

item.title: The role of sample-specific stressors, social identification, stress mindset and resilience for the well-being of descendants of mentally ill parents: a quasi-experimental cross-sectional study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Descendants of mentally ill parents (DMIP) make up about 22% of the population and are 2-13 times more likely to experience mental problems themselves. Preventive health interventions are needed, which should foster protective factors. Unfortunately, little is known about which variables can serve as protective factors for this at-risk group. METHODS: In this quasi-experimental cross-sectional study, we compared DMIP (n = 332) with a control group (n = 90) with mentally healthy parents.

item.title: Clinical spectrum and genetic landscape of MTHFR deficiency: a cohort study including novel variants.
item.description: Methylene tetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) deficiency is a rare inherited metabolic disorder that impairs myelination and brain development, leading to primary clinical manifestations, particularly neurological deficits. The aim of this study was to comprehensively describe the clinical presentation, biochemical profile, and molecular spectrum of patients with MTHFR deficiency. This multicenter, retrospective, descriptive study evaluated the medical records of 19 patients diagnosed with MTHFR deficiency at ten metabolic disease centers. A total of 13 patients had early-onset disease.

item.title: Altered neural prioritization of auditory information during cross-modal attention in children with ADHD.
item.description: Efficient auditory attention requires prioritizing target over nontarget information. Although attentional deficits are a core feature of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), the neural mechanisms underlying auditory prioritization during cross-modal attention remain unclear. We examined neural differentiation between target and nontarget auditory information in children with ADHD.

item.title: Autism spectrum disorder burden in China and worldwide, 1990-2021: A comparative ecological time-series study using global burden of disease 2021 data.
item.description: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) imposes a substantial public health burden. This study quantified and compared the ASD burden in China and globally from 1990 to 2021 to inform policy and planning. We analyzed Global Burden of Disease 2021 estimates of age-standardized prevalence rates (ASPR) and age-standardized disability-adjusted life-year rates (ASDR) in China and worldwide, with analyses by sex and age. Joinpoint regression characterized historical trends.

item.title: Oral health status among preschool children with autism in Changchun, Jilin Province, China: A cross-sectional study.
item.description: This study aimed to compare oral health status, oral-related behaviors, and caregivers' oral-health knowledge and beliefs between preschool children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and typically developing (TD) children. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 694 preschoolers (344 ASD, 350 TD) aged 3-6 in Changchun. Clinical oral examinations were conducted to record caries prevalence and the number of decayed, missing (due to caries), and filled teeth (dmft) index.

item.title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Symptoms in School-Aged Children with a History of Periodic Fever, Aphthous Stomatitis, Pharyngitis, and Cervical Denitis Syndrome: A Comparative Evaluation with Healthy Peers.
item.description: OBJECTIVE: Periodic fever, aphthous stomatitis, pharyngitis, and cervical adenitis (PFAPA) syndrome is the most common periodic fever syndrome of childhood, and growing evidence links early-life inflammation to neurodevelopment, but whether PFAPA affects attention and behavior at school age is unknown. This study compared parent-reported attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms in school-aged children with a preschool PFAPA diagnosis with those of healthy peers and examined associations with PFAPA-related clinical characteristics.

item.title: Rapunzel Syndrome as a Complication of Childhood-Onset Trichotillomania.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Rapunzel syndrome is a rare and potentially life-threatening complication of trichotillomania with trichophagia, characterized by the extension of a gastric trichobezoar into the small intestine. Diagnosis is frequently delayed due to nonspecific presenting symptoms, and management requires both surgical intervention and psychiatric treatment to prevent recurrence. PATIENT CASE: We report the case of a 22-year-old woman with childhood-onset trichotillomania and trichophagia who presented with nonspecific abdominal complaints.

item.title: Association between Maternal Buprenorphine Use and Fetal Head Circumference.
item.description: OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of intrauterine buprenorphine exposure during pregnancy on fetal head circumference. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study reviewed fetal ultrasound reports. Fetal anatomic surveys were typically performed at approximately 20 weeks' gestation. Patients administered medication-assisted treatment (MAT) for opioid use disorder commonly had follow-up estimated fetal weight scans at approximately 32 weeks' gestation due to risks of intrauterine growth restriction.

item.title: Opioid Use Disorder and Evidence-Based Care Among Medicaid-Enrolled Youths.
item.description: IMPORTANCE: One in 100 adolescents and young adults (hereafter "youths") in the US has an opioid use disorder (OUD), yet little is known about the extent to which they receive care aligned with national quality measures. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate progression through the OUD cascade of care (COC) among Medicaid-enrolled youths, with key stages of treatment aligned with national quality measures.

item.title: Distinct Psychological Profiles of Adolescent Psychiatric Outpatients With Non-Suicidal Self-Injury Stratified by Suicidal Ideation.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is a critical clinical marker in early psychiatric intervention for adolescents. It often co-occurs with suicidal ideation (SI), but it remains unclear which component-NSSI or SI-more accurately reflects the underlying psychological burden. METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 417 adolescent outpatients (13-18 years) were classified into four groups: no NSSI/no SI (n = 292), SI without NSSI (n = 66), NSSI without SI (n = 31) and NSSI with SI (n = 28).

item.title: Perinatal mental health equity: patient perspectives on virtual collaborative care providing what women need now in the post-COVID era.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: The COVID-19 pandemic increased perinatal mental health needs and disrupted routine obstetric care, disproportionately affecting Black and economically disadvantaged communities. Michigan's Perinatal Collaborative Care Model (Peri CoCM), a publicly funded virtual program, launched during the pandemic and continued after the public health emergency.

item.title: The role of renin-angiotensin system modulation in the pathophysiology of neuropsychiatric disorders.
item.description: The renin-angiotensin system (RAS), traditionally recognized for cardiovascular and renal regulation, has emerged as a critical mechanistic player in neuropsychiatric pathophysiology. The brain possesses its own independent RAS with components located throughout limbic regions, cortical areas, and monoaminergic circuits that are essential for mood, cognition, and behavior.

item.title: Efficacy of mindfulness-based interventions for children and adolescents with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) reduce core ADHD symptoms and improve neurocognitive or psychosocial outcomes in children and adolescents, synthesizing 14 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) identified through a comprehensive literature search up to December 2025.
FINDINGS: MBIs significantly reduced core ADHD symptoms (SMD = –1.30; 95% CI [–2.14, –0.45]; p = 0.003; I² = 91%). Small but statistically significant improvements were also seen in attention network function (SMD = 0.44; 95% CI [0.01, 0.87]; p = 0.04; I² = 88%) and executive function (SMD = 0.45; 95% CI [0.02, 0.88]; p = 0.04; I² = 84%). No significant effects were found for emotional problems, social problems, externalizing behaviors, or mindfulness skills.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is limited by high statistical heterogeneity (I² > 80% across outcomes) and potential publication bias, which undermines confidence in the pooled estimates. The large SMD for core ADHD symptoms suggests a potentially meaningful clinical effect, but the wide confidence interval and extreme heterogeneity imply inconsistency across studies. The small, heterogeneous effects on neurocognitive domains are of uncertain clinical significance. Overall, the results are preliminary and should be interpreted cautiously until larger, well-controlled RCTs with standardized MBI protocols and active comparators are conducted.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: MBIs may serve as a low-risk adjunctive option for some children with ADHD, particularly to target attention and executive functions, but current evidence does not support their use as a stand-alone treatment or for improving emotional or behavioral outcomes. Clinicians should monitor individual responses and remain alert to the lack of robust, generalizable data.

item.title: Effects of interdisciplinary early developmental intervention programs on behavior, executive functioning and participation in children born preterm: A systematic review with meta-analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review with meta-analysis evaluated whether post-discharge early developmental intervention (EI) programs in preterm-born children improve behavioral outcomes, executive functioning, participation, and other developmental domains. Twenty-six RCTs were included, with seven contributing to meta-analyses.
FINDINGS: Across 11 studies (n=2315), moderate-certainty evidence suggests EI likely has little to no effect on special educational needs. Low-certainty evidence indicates possible small improvements in maternal sensitivity and reductions in behavioral problems in infancy. Very low-certainty evidence exists for attention, language, executive functioning, and medical service use. No studies assessed ADHD, quality of life, or participation outcomes.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is limited by risk of bias (most studies rated as "some concerns" or "high risk") and low to moderate GRADE certainty for key outcomes. While small positive effects on maternal sensitivity and behavioral problems are possible, the clinical significance is uncertain. High-quality, adequately powered RCTs with long-term follow-up are needed to determine whether EI meaningfully changes developmental trajectories in preterm children.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current evidence does not support routine implementation of EI for improving long-term behavioral or developmental outcomes in preterm-born children. Clinicians should remain cautious about overinterpreting small, low-certainty benefits and prioritize evidence-based developmental support within standard care.

item.title: Adaptation and feasibility assessment of a school-based Suicide Prevention Intervention for Adolescents (SPREAD Study) in Nigeria: protocol for a cluster randomised controlled feasibility trial.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The SPREAD study is a cluster randomised controlled feasibility trial in Lagos State, Nigeria, designed to culturally adapt the Youth Aware of Mental Health (YAM) programme for Nigerian secondary schools and assess the feasibility of a future definitive trial. The study addresses the high burden of adolescent suicidal ideation (22.9% lifetime prevalence) in low-resource settings where clinic-based interventions are unsustainable.
FINDINGS: The trial plans to recruit ~600 adolescents aged 13–17 years from 10 public secondary schools, randomised to either the culturally adapted YAM-Nigeria programme (5 sessions) or enhanced usual practice. Primary feasibility outcomes include school recruitment (≥60%), student consent (≥70%), retention at 3-month follow-up (≥75%), implementation fidelity (≥80%), and acceptability (≥70% satisfaction). Secondary outcomes (e.g., suicidal ideation, depression, mental health literacy) will be measured to inform power calculations for a future phase III trial.
INTERPRETATION: This is a well-designed feasibility study with clear progression criteria, addressing a critical gap in adolescent suicide prevention in LMICs. Strengths include the hybrid effectiveness-implementation design and community engagement in adaptation. However, as a feasibility trial, it is not powered to detect clinical efficacy; results will only inform the design of a future definitive trial. External validity may be limited to public secondary schools in Lagos State, and generalisability to other LMIC contexts remains uncertain.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This study does not yet provide clinical evidence for practice change but lays the groundwork for a potential scalable school-based suicide prevention intervention in Nigeria. Clinicians should await results from the definitive trial before considering implementation.

item.title: Antipsychotic Polypharmacy in Hospitalised Adolescents and Young Adults: Predictors, Clinical Correlates and Post-Discharge Outcomes.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This retrospective chart review (N=229) investigated correlates and outcomes of antipsychotic polypharmacy (APP) in psychiatrically hospitalized adolescents and young adults (<25 years) treated for psychosis, addressing a gap in evidence on this population despite guideline recommendations for monotherapy.
FINDINGS: APP occurred in 14% of patients. APP patients had longer hospital stays, more home medications at admission, higher long-acting injectable (LAI) use, and greater documented history of violence. In multivariable logistic regression, history of violence independently predicted APP (OR = 3.30, 95% CI [1.28–8.52]), while absence of LAI at discharge and positive urine drug screening were associated with lower odds. Kaplan–Meier analysis showed no association between APP and one-year readmission risk or time to readmission.
INTERPRETATION: The study suggests APP in youth may reflect acute behavioral risk rather than chronic illness severity, with a moderate independent association for violence (OR ~3.3). However, as a single-center retrospective study, it is prone to selection bias, unmeasured confounding (e.g., illness severity not fully captured), and lacks data on symptom trajectories or functional outcomes. The absence of worse readmission outcomes may reflect careful, time-limited use of APP in high-risk cases, but causality cannot be inferred. Findings are preliminary and should be validated in prospective, multi-site cohorts with standardized outcome measures.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: APP in high-risk youth with psychosis may be selectively justified in acute behavioral crises, but routine or prolonged use lacks supportive outcome data. Clinicians should document clear indications (e.g., violence risk), monitor closely, and prioritize LAI monotherapy where feasible to align with guidelines.

item.title: Flow and Similar Attentional States in Autism and ADHD: A Scoping Review of Similarities and Differences.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The review asks whether attentional states such as hyperfocus, autistic inertia, and monotropism in autistic individuals and those with ADHD resemble or differ from the construct of “flow” (optimal engagement). Using PRISMA-ScR methods, it synthesises 43 publications to map similarities and distinctions.
FINDINGS: Across studies, autistic inertia is described as a barrier to starting or switching tasks, whereas monotropism denotes rigid, narrow focus with repetitive persistence; both diverge from the flexible adaptation seen in typical flow. Hyperfocus shows overlap with flow in intensity and immersion but is often involuntary, lacks clear goals, and is linked to emotional dysregulation. The greatest overlap is between autistic inertia, monotropism, and hyperfocus, suggesting a spectrum of attentional experiences that can shift over time.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is heterogeneous (empirical studies, reviews, conceptual papers) and largely qualitative, so conclusions are suggestive rather than definitive. The review highlights nuanced differences that may inform personalised supports, but effect sizes and quantitative comparisons are not reported. Funding sources and risk of bias assessments are not provided, limiting certainty about internal validity. External validity depends on the representativeness of included samples, which are not clearly described.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Clinicians may use these distinctions to tailor psychoeducation and environmental adaptations (e.g., clear goals, structured transitions) for autistic individuals and those with ADHD, while recognising that attentional states can fluctuate and may yield both productivity gains and risks of rigidity or overload.

item.title: Traditional Chinese medicine health literacy and depressive symptoms in postpartum women: the sequential mediating effects of social support and self-efficacy.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This cross-sectional study in Chengdu, China (Dec 2025–Apr 2026) examined whether Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) health literacy is associated with lower postpartum depressive symptoms, and whether social support and self-efficacy sequentially mediate this relationship in 501 postpartum women.
FINDINGS: TCM health literacy showed a direct negative association with depressive symptoms (β = −0.206, 95% CI −0.299 to −0.112). Three indirect pathways were significant: via social support (β = −0.102, 95% CI −0.167 to −0.050), via self-efficacy (β = −0.102, 95% CI −0.148 to −0.059), and sequentially via social support then self-efficacy (β = −0.033, 95% CI −0.053 to −0.018). The total indirect effect accounted for 53.6% of the total effect.
INTERPRETATION: The study uses a cross-sectional design with convenience sampling, limiting causal inference and generalisability beyond urban Chinese postpartum women. Mediation analyses were pre-specified and bootstrapped, strengthening internal validity, but residual confounding (e.g., prior mental health history) remains possible. The effect sizes are modest; while statistically significant, their clinical magnitude is uncertain without established minimal clinically important differences for these scales.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Findings suggest that enhancing TCM health literacy, social support, and self-efficacy could be targets for postpartum depression prevention, but these hypotheses require confirmation in longitudinal and interventional studies before any bedside changes are warranted.

item.title: Polygenic risk scores as predictors of topiramate's effect in treating alcohol use disorder.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This exploratory machine-learning study (random forest regression) in 278 adults with alcohol use disorder (AUD) from randomized trials asked whether polygenic risk scores (PRS) and clinical features could predict topiramate response and stratify likely responders (LRs) versus unlikely responders (non-LRs).
FINDINGS: The final model retained three predictors: average drinks per day, percent heavy drinking days, and the “Time Until Relapse” PRS, yielding a bias-corrected R² of 0.30. LRs (top four predicted-response quintiles, 80% of the sample) had lower baseline drinking severity and higher “Time Until Relapse” PRS than non-LRs; within LRs, topiramate outperformed placebo on drinking outcomes.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence is preliminary and at high risk of overfitting (single small dataset, internal cross-validation only, no external validation). The PRS contributes modestly beyond strong clinical predictors, and the reported R² of 0.30 does not translate into a clinically meaningful effect size for individual prediction. Confounding by unmeasured sociodemographic or trial-level factors cannot be excluded.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: At present, PRS should not guide topiramate prescribing for AUD; treatment decisions should remain based on clinical severity and patient preference until larger, externally validated models demonstrate reproducible benefit.

item.title: Association between meeting sleep guidelines and anxiety symptoms among Physician assistants in Ghana: a cross-sectional study.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This cross-sectional study investigated whether adherence to recommended sleep duration (7–9 h/night) is associated with lower anxiety symptoms among 439 Physician Assistants in Ghana, addressing a gap in sub-Saharan African healthcare workforce mental health research.
FINDINGS: Only 31.9 % met sleep guidelines; 23.5 % screened positive for anxiety (HADS ≥ 8). In adjusted logistic regression, meeting sleep guidelines was linked to lower odds of anxiety (aOR 0.45, 95 % CI 0.26–0.78). Sensitivity analyses treating sleep as a continuous variable showed a similar inverse association (β –0.69, 95 % CI –1.01 to –0.38). Urban practice doubled the odds of anxiety (aOR 2.17, 95 % CI 1.13–4.16).
INTERPRETATION: The study suggests a modest protective association between adequate sleep and anxiety, but the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. Residual confounding (e.g., workload, shift patterns) and self-reported sleep measures limit internal validity. The effect size (aOR ~0.45) is statistically significant yet moderate; clinical significance in routine care remains uncertain without longitudinal or interventional evidence.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Findings support screening for sleep problems and advocating for healthier work schedules among Ghanaian Physician Assistants, especially in urban settings, while awaiting higher-quality studies to confirm causality and quantify impact on patient care.

item.title: Neuropsychiatric outcomes after montelukast versus inhaled corticosteroids in pediatric asthma: a pooled birth cohort study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The evidence regarding montelukast‑associated neuropsychiatric adverse events in children with asthma is controversial and inconclusive. We sought to further examine the association between use of montelukast and the risk of neuropsychiatric events in children with asthma. METHODS: We conducted a pooled analysis of two birth cohorts: the AMerican PREGNANcy-Mother-Child CohorT (AM-PREGNANT) from the US, and the Quebec Pregnancy Cohort (QPC) from Canada.

item.title: Umbrella Review of Meta-Analyses of Comprehensive Applied Behavior Analytic Interventions for Young Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
item.description: PURPOSE: The purpose of this review was to conduct an umbrella review of systematic reviews with meta-analytic syntheses of comprehensive applied behavior analytic interventions for young autistic children. METHOD: We searched six electronic databases and conducted supplemental searches through December 2025. We examined two primary outcomes (IQ, adaptive behavior) and four secondary outcomes (communication, social, daily living skills, and symptomatology), conducted assessments for risks of bias, and examined primary study overlap using the corrected covered area (CCA).

item.title: Meta-analysis prompt guided multi-task graph transformer for joint analysis of cognitive deficits and psychiatric disorders.
item.description: Psychiatric disorders, such as schizophrenia and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), are associated with altered functional connectivity (FC) and are often accompanied by cognitive deficits. Leveraging the shared neural mechanisms underlying both psychiatric disorders and cognitive impairment may improve diagnostic accuracy. However, due to the complexity and heterogeneity of these conditions, diagnosis based on FC alone remains challenging in terms of accuracy and biomarker reliability.

item.title: From lack of assertiveness to depression: A co-twin control study of hostility and social support across 23 years.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Although lack of assertiveness (LOA) and hostility are established risk factors for depression, the mechanisms linking them to depression and their genetic or environmental contributions remain unclear. We used the Swedish Adoption/Twin Study of Aging (SATSA) to test whether social support (SS) deficits mediated these pathways. METHODS: Community-dwelling twins (N = 2,034; 1,017 pairs) were followed for up to 23 years (1984-2007). We examined serial (LOA → hostility → SS → depression) and parallel (LOA + hostility → SS → depression) mediation models.

item.title: Estimating trends in serious psychological distress and depression among 18- to 64-year-olds in the United States from 2004 to 2019 using K6 and PHQ scales.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Information from large national surveys is potentially useful for examining trends in mental health, but prior research has obtained inconsistent findings. This study attempts to determine whether Kessler 6 and Patient Health Questionnaire measures from different surveys consistently indicate trends in serious psychological distress or depression.

item.title: Methylphenidate treatment status and subclinical atherosclerosis in children and adolescents with ADHD: a cross-sectional comparative study.
item.description: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has been increasingly associated with chronic inflammation and may contribute to early cardiovascular risk. Although subclinical atherosclerosis has been documented in drug-naive children with ADHD, whether methylphenidate treatment status is associated with differences in subclinical atherosclerotic markers remains unknown. This study aimed to evaluate the association between methylphenidate treatment status and subclinical atherosclerosis in children and adolescents with ADHD.

item.title: End-to-end deep learning methods for genetic risk prediction of schizophrenia.
item.description: Schizophrenia is a highly heritable psychiatric disorder with a complex genetic basis. While recent GWAS and whole exome sequencing studies have identified numerous risk loci, existing clinical prediction models rely primarily on linear assumptions, limiting their ability to capture complex, nonlinear genetic effects such as epistasis. In this study, we apply end-to-end genome interpretation neural network models to predict schizophrenia risk using whole exome sequencing data in a cohort of 6,135 cases and 6,245 controls.

item.title: The Impact of Sexual Satisfaction on Marital Adjustment, Quality of Life, and Treatment Adherence in Patients Diagnosed With Bipolar Disorder and Their Spouses: A Cross-Sectional Study.
item.description: OBJECTIVES: To examine the effects of sexual satisfaction on marital adjustment, quality of life, and treatment adherence in patients diagnosed with bipolar disorder (BD) and their spouses. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 124 euthymic patients with BD and their spouses (124 couples; n = 248 individuals), recruited from the psychiatry outpatient clinics of Gaziantep University Şahinbey Research and Practice Hospital, Türkiye.

item.title: Emotional and Behavioral Problems Among Siblings of Children With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in a Tertiary Child Psychiatry Setting in Bangladesh: A Cross-Sectional Study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Siblings of children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) may experience emotional and behavioral difficulties. Shared genetic and environmental factors, family stress, caregiving demands, and potentially unequal parental attention may contribute to these difficulties. However, the mental health needs of these siblings may be overlooked. METHODS: This cross-sectional descriptive study included 95 siblings aged 4-17 years of children with ADHD attending the Department of Psychiatry, BSMMU.

item.title: Global, regional, and national burden of schizophrenia and its environmental drivers, 1990-2021: Retrospective analysis and projections to 2040.
item.description: Given the global prevalence of schizophrenia (SCZ), it is urgent to elucidate and quantify its burden and clarify its environmental and social influencing factors. This study aimed to quantify the global disease burden of SCZ. It also investigated the causes of regional disparities and the impact of environmental and social factors. This study conducted an extensive analysis of the global, regional and national incidence, prevalence, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of SCZ. In 2021, there were 1.22 million incident cases, 23.18 million prevalent cases and 14.82 million DALYs.

item.title: From voxels to models: a multi-center voxel-based morphometry study identifying robust biomarkers for deep learning classification of schizophrenia.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The application of deep learning in psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia has lagged behind neuro-oncology, primarily due to a lack of identifiable neuroanatomical targets and concerns regarding generalizability across sites. METHODS: To address this, we analyzed structural MRI data from a multi-site study of 401 subjects (194 schizophrenia, 207 healthy) across three independent datasets (COBRE, FBIRN, SLIM).

item.title: Shared genetic architecture of schizophrenia and lupus identifies pleiotropic loci with distinct downstream mechanisms.
item.description: Schizophrenia (SCZ) and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) exhibit epidemiological overlap, suggesting shared genetic underpinnings. Using the largest SLE genome-wide association study (GWAS) to date, we identified a significant genetic correlation between SCZ and SLE (rg = 0.25, p = 9.0 × 10-4). Cross-trait analysis nominated multiple candidate shared loci outside the major histocompatibility complex (MHC), most with aligned effects. The strongest candidate shared association was found at the FURIN-FES locus, previously implicated in SCZ and newly associated with SLE.

item.title: Associations between anemia and postpartum depression among Arab Bedouin women.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Anemia and postpartum depression (PPD) are common perinatal morbidities. Recognition of postpartum anemia as a major risk factor for PPD is crucial for postpartum maternal health. This study aimed to examine the association between anemia and PPD in low-income minority Arab-Bedouin mothers in southern Israel. METHODS: The study was conducted in 2017-2018 and included 332 women aged 18 to 45 years who were 2-4 months postpartum. Retrospective data on postpartum anemia (defined as a hemoglobin level < 12 g/dL) was extracted from women's medical records in the clinics.

item.title: Fronto-cingulate gamma synchrony predicts deep brain stimulation response in treatment-resistant depression: preliminary evidence.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Gamma-band activity has been linked to cognitive-affective processing in depression. However, its role in deep brain stimulation (DBS) response in treatment-resistant depression (TRD) remains unclear. This exploratory study investigated whether ventral capsule/ventral striatum DBS (VCVS-DBS) modulates gamma activity during cognitive-affective processing and whether DBS-related gamma changes are associated with improvement in depressive symptoms. METHODS: Seven participants with TRD completed an affective Multi-Source Interference Task during DBS ON and OFF.

item.title: PTSD Is Associated With Severity of Upper GI Symptoms in Patients With Gastroparesis.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Posttraumatic stress disorder may contribute to chronic overactivation of the sympathetic nervous system and exacerbate GI symptoms. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the impacts of PTSD on GI symptom severity and psychological functioning in patients with gastroparesis. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of gastroparesis patients at a tertiary care center. Patients completed questionnaires at the initial evaluation. Objective markers of gastric function were extracted from the medical record.

item.title: Age-stratified safety signal mining of ADHD medications in pediatric populations using the FAERS database (2014-2024): a pharmacovigilance study using multi-method disproportionality analysis.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Pediatric attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) medications have been analyzed in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), yet systematic age-stratified signal profiling under ICH E11(R1) developmental categories, covering the recently approved agents viloxazine and serdexmethylphenidate, remains unreported. METHODS: We performed a retrospective disproportionality analysis of pediatric (age <18 years) FAERS reports, 2014Q1-2024Q4, after FDA-standard three-step deduplication.

item.title: The asymmetric relationship of parental psychological flexibility and parenting involvement in autism: anxiety as a mediator.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Parents of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) face immense pressure and challenges. In traditional Chinese culture, a distinct division of labor exists, with mothers typically bearing greater parenting burdens. This study examined the relationship between parental psychological flexibility (PPF) and parental involvement in families of children with ASD, investigated the mediating role of anxiety, and explored the interaction effects between parents. METHODS: The study included 83 pairs of parents of children with ASD.
